finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches an attacker-supplied URL. The only host check is a bare suffix match (endswith 'example.com' with no leading dot), so any registrable domain ending in 'example.com' passes, e.g. 'evilexample.com' or 'attacker-example.com'. Nothing checks the resolved IP, so a passing name can resolve to 127.0.0.1, RFC1918 space, or 169.254.169.254. The response length is returned to the caller, so this is a blind/side-channel SSRF.

trace.note: url: str taken from the query string, unconstrained
host = urlparse(url).hostname or '' extracts the hostname
if not host.endswith('example.com'): bare suffix check, no leading dot, so 'evilexample.com' passes. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 ('.example.com') is defined but unused
c.get(url) requests the original, unvalidated URL string; name is resolved by the server, so DNS can point to internal addresses
returns only len(r.text), limiting the data leak to response length

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check at line 13: present but insufficient (matches evilexample.com, attacker-example.com). Scheme: not checked, but httpx only handles http/https so file:// fails. Resolved IP / private-range / metadata-address blocking: absent. Redirects: httpx does not follow them by default in current versions, which blocks redirect-based bypass; this depends on version (older httpx followed redirects by default). Port restriction: absent. /ping (lines 20-24) uses a hardcoded URL and is not a sink. Unverified: urlparse vs httpx parser differentials (e.g. backslash or @ tricks such as 'http://evil.com\@example.com') were not tested and depend on the installed httpx version.

verdict.guard_found: Only the bare suffix check at mirror.py:13 (`host.endswith("example.com")`), which does not close the finding: it accepts evilexample.com and attacker-example.com. No IP, private-range, metadata, scheme, or port restriction exists, and ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is unused.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter (mirror.py:11) is unauthenticated attacker input, urlparse().hostname (mirror.py:12) yields "evilexample.com" for a hostile URL, which passes the suffix check at mirror.py:13, and c.get(url) at mirror.py:16 fetches it with default settings, returning only len(r.text) at mirror.py:17, so the SSRF is blind. The trace matches the file exactly; the httpx parser-differential part of the claim was not needed to confirm it.
